source.check: returned unopposed: the Impartial Reporter of 21 May 1964 (p. 7) reports that Mr. Thornton, a Unionist, 'takes the place of Mr. Matthew McHugh for the Kinglass division' at the close of nominations; no contest for the council

note: Triennial election of Enniskillen Rural District Council, polled Thursday 4 June 1964. There was no contest, but four changes in personnel were reported: Ivan Loane replaced Richard Thornton at a Unionist delegates' meeting for Lisbofin, John James Nixon replaced Thomas Bothwell for Coolyermore, John R. Leonard filled the vacant Holywell seat, and the sitting Kinglass member, Mr. Mathew McHugh, was not nominated. The Impartial Reporter of 21 May 1964, p. 7, reports the full nominations: Mr. Richard Thornton (Unionist), passed over for Lisbofin, 'takes the place of Mr. Matthew McHugh for the Kinglass division', and names the members for 'the 22 other seats [which] remain unchanged'. All twenty-six divisions are filled from that report (6 Nov 2026). Mr. Richard Thornton, secretary of the County Fermanagh Grand Orange Lodge, was not re-selected for Lisbofin, which he had represented for nine years, and was nominated instead for the Nationalist-held Kinglass seat (headline 'Unionist Gets Nationalist Seat'). Returned unopposed.
